assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron tunneling through proteins is a physical mechanism stated in quantitative terms: distance and driving-force dependence of rates, tunneling pathways, and hopping through aromatic residues. It underpins biological energy conversion, including respiratory chain enzymes and photosynthesis, and is the kind of mechanism-first biophysical chemistry I value most.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the clear core, with a long joint record of experiments on ruthenium-modified proteins. Parallel theory of tunneling pathways by others is not credited here, so the pair is a fair two-person configuration for the experimental demonstration.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and textbook status, so recognition is, if anything, late. Interpretation of tunneling versus hopping is stable.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would want the theoretical foundations (Marcus-type theory, already recognized in 1992) credited separately; as I recall, not independently verified here.
Expert reports would need to confirm that priority is not split with other protein-ET groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the central enzyme of biological nitrogen fixation. Structures of the FeMo cofactor, including the central carbide and the later turnover-state structures, combined with kinetic and spectroscopic mechanism, give a chemically deep and fundamental picture of one of the hardest reactions in biology.
assessment.attribution: Rees provided the first structures and cofactor architecture, Einsle the atomic-resolution cofactor with interstitial carbide, and Seefeldt the kinetic and mechanistic framework. Dean, Ribbe and others have strong claims, so the three-person limit forces a contested choice.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well confirmed over decades. The full catalytic mechanism, including N2 binding and hydride chemistry, is still debated, so recognition could be seen as somewhat early for mechanism but not for structure.
uncertainties: Which of Rees, Einsle, Dean, Seefeldt, Ribbe is decisive is unresolved.
The catalytic cycle is incompletely settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling is a widely used method in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, with ligand design grounded in mechanism. The 2010 prize on cross-coupling did not cover this chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general, ligand-enabled amination, building on the earlier tin-amide work credited to Kosugi. A two-laureate prize is natural, with Kosugi's earlier precedent a possible priority question.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, with industrial adoption and extensive independent confirmation. Timing is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make some members reluctant.
Priority relative to Migita and Kosugi work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional and isotope-labeled NMR plus relaxation methods made structures and dynamics of large biomolecules accessible in solution, showing motion and exchange as part of function. This is a method that made mechanisms visible.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore have the most decisive methodological contributions in my recollection; Wagner and Palmer are also strong, so selection is difficult and the field might be better treated as a line of work than one discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted. NMR was recognized in 2002 (Wüthrich), which may be seen as a partial precedent.
uncertainties: Risk that this is a line of work with diffuse credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a core concept connecting theory, molecular electrocatalysis and biological enzymes, directly relevant to proton pumping and redox enzymes that I know well. It provides a physical framework for coupled proton and electron motion.
assessment.attribution: Mayer and Hammes-Schiffer are strongest conceptually and theoretically; Nocera contributed model systems and energy catalysis. Meyer's early work is also relevant. Credit is spread, and I would flag that.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are widely accepted and used in biology and catalysis. Quantitative understanding in complex enzymes is still developing.
uncertainties: Distribution of credit among four names, with Meyer excluded by the limit of three.
Candidacy rests on a conceptual line of work rather than a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at free-electron lasers gives room-temperature, damage-free structures and time-resolved snapshots of reactions, which is the visualization of dynamics in 3D that links structure to kinetics.
assessment.attribution: Chapman provided the diffraction-before-destruction principle and data methods, Fromme the first serial crystallography demonstration with photosystem I, and Schlichting time-resolved applications. Hajdu's role is significant, and I am not certain of his current status.
assessment.maturity: Core method confirmed, but many time-resolved chemical results are still emerging, so recognition may be a few years early.
uncertainties: Many mechanistic claims from time-resolved studies still need independent confirmation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry reveals composition, stoichiometry and interactions of intact membrane and soluble complexes, including respiratory assemblies. It adds a distinct and chemically important capability.
assessment.attribution: Robinson and Heck are leading figures; earlier foundations by Chait, Loo and Gross are real, so the credit allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Methodology is mature and adopted, though mass spectrometry already received a prize in 2002.
uncertainties: Heck also appears in proteomics, which may blur the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite solar cells reached high efficiency very quickly and changed photovoltaics research, with new questions about charge transport and defects.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka made the first perovskite sensitized cell, Park and Snaith the solid-state high-efficiency devices; Kanatzidis, Grätzel and Seok also have claims, so the three-laureate limit is a real problem.
assessment.maturity: Efficiencies are broadly reproduced, but stability and toxicity are unresolved, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and commercial viability are unproven.
Contested priority among six credited names.
